text:
Marathon Petroleum stock jumped 3.7% today as oil prices spiked on geopolitical tension in the Middle East. A Saudi Arabian pipeline that moves crude internally was damaged in a drone attack, and while U.S. officials said repairs would take only days, analysts warned that if the shutdown lasts longer than a week, oil prices could rally sharply—which would boost refiner margins. The stock has now climbed 10% in two weeks as these regional risks have built; U.S. crude is trading at $97 per barrel and world crude at $109, well above typical levels.

Refineries are running at 97.8% capacity, meaning the industry is operating near maximum and can capture more profit from each barrel processed when crude costs more relative to finished fuel prices. With limited spare production capacity globally and uncertainty about how long the Saudi pipeline outage will last, the market is pricing in the possibility of sustained high energy costs—exactly the environment where a major refiner like this one tends to perform well.
